claim: Stentor coeruleus is a giant ciliate that is a classical model system for studying regeneration and morphogenesis in a single cell.
source: The giant ciliate Stentor coeruleus is a classical model system for studying regeneration and morphogenesis in a single cell.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an introductory statement about the organism.

claim: The oral apparatus of Stentor can be induced to shed and regenerate in a series of reproducible morphological steps.
source: The anterior of the cell is marked by an array of cilia, known as the oral apparatus, which can be induced to shed and regenerate in a series of reproducible morphological steps, previously shown to require transcription.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Oral apparatus regeneration requires transcription.
source: The anterior of the cell is marked by an array of cilia, known as the oral apparatus, which can be induced to shed and regenerate in a series of reproducible morphological steps, previously shown to require transcription.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and referenced to prior work.

claim: When a Stentor cell is cut in half, each half regenerates an intact cell.
source: If a cell is cut in half, each half regenerates an intact cell.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract.

claim: RNA sequencing was used to assay dynamic changes in Stentor's transcriptome during regeneration after both oral apparatus shedding and bisection.
source: We used RNA sequencing (RNAseq) to assay the dynamic changes in Stentor's transcriptome during regeneration, after both oral apparatus shedding and bisection, allowing us to identify distinct temporal waves of gene expression including kinases, RNA -binding proteins, centriole biogenesis factors, and orthologs of human ciliopathy genes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a description of the methods used.

claim: Distinct temporal waves of gene expression during regeneration include kinases, RNA-binding proteins, centriole biogenesis factors, and orthologs of human ciliopathy genes.
source: We used RNA sequencing (RNAseq) to assay the dynamic changes in Stentor's transcriptome during regeneration, after both oral apparatus shedding and bisection, allowing us to identify distinct temporal waves of gene expression including kinases, RNA -binding proteins, centriole biogenesis factors, and orthologs of human ciliopathy genes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the RNAseq analysis.

claim: Comparing transcriptional profiles of different regeneration events identified distinct modules of gene expression corresponding to oral apparatus regeneration, posterior holdfast regeneration, and recovery after wounding.
source: By comparing transcriptional profiles of different regeneration events, we identified distinct modules of gene expression corresponding to oral apparatus regeneration, posterior holdfast regeneration, and recovery after wounding.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from comparative analysis.

claim: Sequential waves of gene expression involve a cascade mechanism in which later waves of expression are triggered by translation products of early-expressed genes.
source: By measuring gene expression after blocking translation, we show that the sequential waves of gene expression involve a cascade mechanism in which later waves of expression are triggered by translation products of early-expressed genes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from cycloheximide experiments.

claim: An E2F transcription factor and the RNA-binding protein Pumilio were identified as potential regulators of regeneration based on the expression pattern of their predicted target genes.
source: Among the early-expressed genes, we identified an E2F transcription factor and the RNA-binding protein Pumilio as potential regulators of regeneration based on the expression pattern of their predicted target genes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from analysis of early-expressed genes.

claim: Pumilio is required for regenerating oral structures of the correct size.
source: RNAi-mediated knockdown experiments indicate that Pumilio is required for regenerating oral structures of the correct size.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from RNAi experiments.

claim: E2F is involved in the completion of regeneration but is dispensable for earlier steps.
source: E2F is involved in the completion of regeneration but is dispensable for earlier steps.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from RNAi experiments.

claim: Removal of the macronucleus at any stage causes oral apparatus regeneration to halt at the next stage.
source: Removal of the macronucleus, at any stage, causes OA regeneration to halt at the next stage, suggesting that several waves of gene expression may be required to drive different processes at different stages (Tartar, 1961).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Tartar 1961.

claim: Several waves of gene expression may be required to drive different processes at different stages of oral apparatus regeneration.
source: Removal of the macronucleus, at any stage, causes OA regeneration to halt at the next stage, suggesting that several waves of gene expression may be required to drive different processes at different stages (Tartar, 1961).
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the macronucleus removal experiments.

claim: Each Stentor cell contains multiple micronuclei that are closely adjacent to the macronucleus.
source: In addition to the macronucleus, each Stentor cell contains multiple micronuclei, which are generally not visible because they are closely adjacent to the macronucleus.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background information.

claim: Micronuclei are required for sexual reproduction but are dispensable for regeneration and for mitotic cell division.
source: The micronuclei are required for sexual reproduction but are dispensable for regeneration and for mitotic cell division (Schwartz, 1935; Tartar, 1961).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Chemical inhibitor studies showed that regeneration of the oral apparatus requires transcription.
source: Chemical inhibitor studies showed that regeneration of the OA requires transcription (Whitson, 1965; James, 1967; Burchill, 1968; Younger et al., 1972) and it is also known that overall levels of RNA synthesis increase several fold during the OA regeneration process (Ellwood and Cowden, 1966; Burchill, 1968; Younger et al., 1972).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Overall levels of RNA synthesis increase several fold during the oral apparatus regeneration process.
source: Chemical inhibitor studies showed that regeneration of the OA requires transcription (Whitson, 1965; James, 1967; Burchill, 1968; Younger et al., 1972) and it is also known that overall levels of RNA synthesis increase several fold during the OA regeneration process (Ellwood and Cowden, 1966; Burchill, 1968; Younger et al., 1972).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: The oral apparatus is a prominent structure on the anterior side of the cell that contains thousands of basal bodies and cilia organized into a ciliated ring known as a membranellar band.
source: The OA is a prominent structure on the anterior side of the cell that contains thousands of basal bodies and cilia (Paulin and Bussey, 1971) organized into a ciliated ring known as a membranellar band (MB).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work.

claim: The oral apparatus can be induced to shed using sucrose shock, after which a new oral apparatus regenerates over the course of 8 hours.
source: The OA can be induced to shed using sucrose shock (Tartar, 1957) after which a new OA regenerates over the course of 8 hr, progressing through a series of well-characterized morphological stages (Figure 1A; Tartar, 1961).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: When a Stentor cell is cut in half along its longitudinal axis, the posterior half regenerates a new oral apparatus while the anterior half regenerates a new tail.
source: When a Stentor cell is cut in half along its longitudinal axis, the posterior half regenerates a new OA, while the anterior half regenerates a new tail (Morgan, 1901b).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Morgan 1901b.

claim: Both halves of a bisected Stentor cell are able to regenerate because the elongated macronucleus is divided into both halves during surgery and is highly polyploid.
source: Both fragments are able to regenerate because the elongated macronucleus that is divided into both halves during surgery is highly polyploid, ensuring that each half-cell retains many copies of the genome.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1B caption.

claim: 4323 genes exhibited dynamic expression patterns through regeneration in sucrose-shocked cells.
source: Overall, we identified 4323 genes that exhibited dynamic expression patterns through regeneration in sucrose-shocked cells, 1020 in posterior half-cells following bisection, and 229 in anterior half-cells following bisection.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the RNAseq analysis.

claim: 1020 genes exhibited dynamic expression patterns through regeneration in posterior half-cells following bisection.
source: Overall, we identified 4323 genes that exhibited dynamic expression patterns through regeneration in sucrose-shocked cells, 1020 in posterior half-cells following bisection, and 229 in anterior half-cells following bisection.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the RNAseq analysis.

claim: 229 genes exhibited dynamic expression patterns through regeneration in anterior half-cells following bisection.
source: Overall, we identified 4323 genes that exhibited dynamic expression patterns through regeneration in sucrose-shocked cells, 1020 in posterior half-cells following bisection, and 229 in anterior half-cells following bisection.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the RNAseq analysis.

claim: In total, 4811 differentially expressed genes were detected, which constitutes roughly 10% of the Stentor genome.
source: In total we detected 4811 differentially expressed genes, which constitutes roughly 10% of the Stentor genome.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the RNAseq analysis.

claim: The anterior half-cells showed by far the smallest number of differentially expressed genes, while the sucrose-shocked cells showed the largest.
source: The anterior half-cells showed by far the smallest number of differentially expressed genes, while the sucrose-shocked cells showed the largest.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a comparison of the three datasets.

claim: Among the annotated genes in the oral apparatus-specific set, many were found that are related to centriole biogenesis.
source: Among the annotated genes in the OA-specific set (Supplementary file 1), many were found that are related to centriole biogenesis, in keeping with the fact that a large number of new basal bodies form during OA regeneration in order to act as basal bodies for the cilia of the MB of the OA.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of the OA-specific gene set.

claim: Most centriole-related genes are expressed in clusters 2 and 3, during the period when thousands of new basal bodies are being formed de novo.
source: It is notable that most of these are expressed in clusters 2 and 3, consisting of genes whose expression peaks at 1.5–2 hr after sucrose shock, during the period of time at which the first evidence of an oral primordium becomes visible in scanning electron microscopy (Paulin and Bussey, 1971), and at which transmission electron microscopy reveals that thousands of new basal bodies are being formed de novo, creating a so-called 'anarchic field' (Bernard and Bohatier, 1981).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior microscopy studies.

claim: Among the upregulated centriole-related genes are SAS6, SAS4, POC1, CETN3, CETN2, CEP76, CEP135, and CEP120.
source: Among the upregulated genes are SAS6, SAS4, POC1,CETN3, CETN2, CEP76, CEP135, CEP120.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as examples of upregulated centriole genes.

claim: SAS6 is one of the earliest known factors involved in assembling the ninefold symmetric structure of the centriole.
source: SAS6 is notable as one of the earliest known factors involved in assembling the ninefold symmetric structure of the centriole (Leidel et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: Out of the 29 most conserved ancestral centriole genes, 10 are expressed in either cluster 2 or 3.
source: Out of the 29 most conserved ancestral centriole genes, we find that 10 are expressed in either cluster 2 or 3.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of conserved centriole genes.

claim: One centriole-related gene, LRC45, is expressed later than the others in cluster 4.
source: One centriole-related gene, LRC45, is expressed later than the others in cluster 4.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation about timing of gene expression.

claim: Almost no genes encoding components of the motile ciliary machinery were differentially expressed in the oral apparatus-specific module.
source: A handful of genes involved in ciliary assembly are expressed in later clusters, including several IFT proteins, but almost no genes encoding components of the motile ciliary machinery were differentially expressed in any cluster.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation about the OA-specific module.

claim: The sucrose shock-specific module includes 12 of the 29 ancestral centriole genes.
source: Genes upregulated during sucrose shock response included 12 of the 29 ancestral centriole genes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of the sucrose shock-specific module.

claim: Clusters 3 and 4 of the sucrose shock-specific gene set contain a large number of genes that encode protein components of motile cilia.
source: In stark contrast to the lack of cilia-related genes in the OA-specific gene set presented above, we found that clusters 3 and 4 of the sucrose shock-specific gene set contain a large number of genes that encode proteins components of motile cilia.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of the sucrose shock-specific module.

claim: Expression of genes encoding components of the inner and outer dynein arms are seen across clusters 2, 3, and 4 of the sucrose shock-specific module.
source: Expression of genes encoding components of the inner and outer dynein arms, which power ciliary motility, are seen across clusters 2, 3, and 4.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of the sucrose shock-specific module.

claim: Genes encoding the dynein regulatory complex are expressed exclusively during cluster 3.
source: Genes encoding the dynein regulatory complex are expressed exclusively during cluster 3 (DRC 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, and 11).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of the sucrose shock-specific module.

claim: Expression of genes encoding radial spoke components begins in cluster 3 and is most apparent in cluster 4.
source: Expression of genes encoding radial spoke components begins in cluster 3 and is most apparent in cluster 4, where eight radial spoke proteins are expressed (RSP1, 3, 4, 7, 9, 10, 14, and 16).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of the sucrose shock-specific module.

claim: The peak expression of genes encoding centriole proteins occurs earlier than the peak expression of genes encoding motile cilia proteins.
source: Overall, we observe that the peak expression of genes encoding centriole proteins occurs earlier than the peak expression of genes encoding motile cilia proteins (compare Figure 2E and F), which is consistent with the fact that ciliogenesis takes place later than basal body biogenesis in Stentor.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2E and F.

claim: The timing of cluster 4 gene expression correlates with the time period during which the oral cilia transition from random beating to coordinated beating forming metachronal waves.
source: The timing of group 4 also correlates with the time period during which the oral cilia transition from their initial random beating motility to their characteristic coordinated beating motility, forming metachronal waves (Paulin and Bussey, 1971; Wan et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claim: The bisection-specific genes are shared between half-cells that are regenerating distinct structures.
source: The bisection-specific genes (Figure 3B) are shared between half-cells that are regenerating distinct structures.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: The bisection-specific differential gene expression pattern reflects a response to physical wounding of the cell.
source: We therefore interpret the bisection-specific differential gene expression pattern as reflecting a response to physical wounding of the cell.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the bisection-specific module.

claim: Direct measurements of membrane integrity in Stentor indicate that the plasma membrane seals itself on a time scale of 100–1000 seconds after wounding.
source: Direct measurements of membrane integrity in Stentor indicate that the plasma membrane seals itself on a time scale of 100–1000 s after wounding (Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: The upregulated genes in the bisection response peak at 120–240 minutes after wounding, long after the wound itself has been closed.
source: In comparison, the upregulated genes in the bisection response peak at 120–240 min after wounding, long after the wound itself has been closed.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a comparison of timing.

claim: The bisection-specific transcriptional module is more likely to reflect recovery of cell state after wound closure, rather than the wound closure process itself.
source: Thus, the bisection-specific transcriptional module is more likely to reflect recovery of cell state after wound closure, rather than the wound closure process itself.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation based on timing.

claim: Two of the upregulated genes in the bisection-specific module encode ammonium transporters, and a third encodes carbonic anhydrase.
source: Two of the upregulated genes in the bisection-specific module encode ammonium transporters, and a third encodes carbonic anhydrase.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of the bisection-specific module.

claim: Ammonium transporters and carbonic anhydrase work together to control pH of both blood and cytoplasm in animals.
source: In animals, ammonium transporters and carbonic anhydrase work together to control pH of both blood and cytoplasm (Weiner and Verlander, 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: A key function of the bisection-specific transcriptional module is restoration of proper intracellular pH once the membrane rupture has been healed.
source: We infer that a key function of the bisection-specific transcriptional module is restoration of proper intracellular pH once the membrane rupture has been healed.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference based on the genes expressed.

claim: Out of the 431 genes that show differential expression in the oral apparatus-specific regeneration module, 21 genes (5% of the total) were completely unaffected by cycloheximide treatment.
source: Out of the 431 genes that show differential expression in the OA-specific regeneration module (Figure 2A), we found that 21 genes, constituting only 5% of the total gene set, were completely unaffected by cycloheximide treatment as judged by a high correlation coefficient in expression profiles with and without cycloheximide (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4C.

claim: The remaining 411 genes (95% of the total) in the oral apparatus-specific module had their expression affected to varying degrees by cycloheximide treatment.
source: The remaining 411 genes (95% of the total) had their expression affected to varying degrees as judged by a reduction in the correlation with their untreated expression pattern (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4D.

claim: The largest effects of cycloheximide treatment were seen in cluster 1 (genes that are repressed during regeneration) and in clusters 4 and 5 (genes that are upregulated late in regeneration).
source: Based on these average correlation coefficients, the largest effects, corresponding to the lowest correlations, were seen in cluster 1, consisting of genes that normally are repressed during regeneration, and in clusters 4 and 5, consisting of genes that normally are upregulated late in regeneration.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of cycloheximide effects.

claim: The majority of the genes unaffected by cycloheximide treatment are contained in cluster 2, the earliest expressing cluster.
source: Consistent with this view, the majority of the genes unaffected by cycloheximide treatment are contained in cluster 2, the earliest expressing cluster, while the loss of expression in cycloheximide-treated cells is most dramatic in clusters 4 and 5, the latest-expressing clusters.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of cycloheximide effects.

claim: Treatment of regenerating Stentor cells with cycloheximide leads to arrest of regeneration if treated within the first 4–5 hours.
source: It has previously been shown that treatment of regenerating Stentor cells with cycloheximide leads to arrest of regeneration if treated within the first 4–5 hr, whereas when cycloheximide is added at later times it causes a delay in the final stages but does not fully prevent regeneration (Burchill, 1968; Younger et al., 1972).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claim: A search for transcription factors in the oral apparatus-specific cluster 2 revealed the transcription factor E2F, as well as its dimerization partner E2FDP1, and several alleles of Rb.
source: A search for transcription factors in the OA-specific cluster 2, which consists of the earliest genes to be upregulated during OA regeneration, revealed the transcription factor E2F, as well as its dimerization partner E2FDP1, and several alleles of Rb, a regulator of the E2F-DP1 interaction.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of cluster 2 genes.

claim: The Rb-E2F-DP1 module plays important roles in regulating cell cycle-dependent processes in many species.
source: The Rb-E2F-DP1 module plays important roles in regulating cell cycle-dependent processes in many species (Bertoli et al., 2013; Nair et al., 2009), including Tetrahymena and Chlamydomonas (Zhang et al., 2018. Cross, 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claim: E2F is upregulated in oral apparatus-regenerating cells even if they are treated with cycloheximide.
source: Importantly, E2F is upregulated in OA-regenerating cells even if they are treated with cycloheximide, consistent with a possible role as an early gene that may serve as a regulator of later expression waves.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from cycloheximide experiments.

claim: There is a tight pattern of E2F targets expressed during a 1 hour window that corresponds roughly to the time in regeneration at which centriole-related genes are expressed.
source: As shown in Figure 5B, there is indeed a tight pattern of E2F targets expressed during a 1 hr window that corresponds roughly to the time in regeneration at which centriole-related genes are expressed (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5B and Figure 2E.

claim: There are 13 predicted E2F targets among the oral apparatus-specific genes.
source: Based on the data annotated in this table, there are 13 predicted E2F targets, of which only one, SteCoe_2152, showed normal expression when cells were treated with cycloheximide.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from promoter motif analysis.

claim: The majority (10/13) of the E2F targets are in cluster 2.
source: The majority (10/13) of the E2F targets are in cluster 2, two are in cluster 3, and one is in cluster 5.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of E2F targets.

claim: None of the predicted E2F targets are found in cluster 1 consisting of genes that are repressed during regeneration.
source: None of the predicted E2F targets are found in cluster 1 consisting of genes that are repressed during regeneration, suggesting that E2F likely plays an activating function in this process.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of E2F targets.

claim: E2F likely plays an activating function in the regeneration process.
source: None of the predicted E2F targets are found in cluster 1 consisting of genes that are repressed during regeneration, suggesting that E2F likely plays an activating function in this process.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference based on the distribution of E2F targets.

claim: The target list of E2F in Stentor includes cyclin and cyclin-associated protein A.
source: However, consistent with the role of E2F in regulating cyclin transcription in other organisms, the target list in Stentor does include cyclin and cyclin-associated protein A.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of E2F targets.

claim: In E2F RNAi-treated cells, the oral primordium formed normally after sucrose shock but failed to progress or be maintained.
source: In E2F RNAi-treated cells, the oral primordium formed normally after sucrose shock (compare Figure 5C versus Figure 5G), but failed to progress or be maintained, such that by 8 hr, a large fraction of cells were missing either an oral primordium or fully developed OA (Figure 5E versus Figure 5I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5 panels.

claim: Oral regeneration proceeds normally for the first 4 hours in E2F RNAi cells, but then fails to proceed in later time points.
source: Taken together, our results indicate that oral regeneration proceeds normally for the first 4 hr, but then fails to proceed in later time points (Figure 5K).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5K.

claim: The loss of oral primordia at later stages in E2F RNAi cells is reminiscent of the loss of oral primordia in regenerating cells from which the nucleus is removed.
source: The loss of oral primordia at later stages is reminiscent of the loss of oral primordia in regenerating cells from which the nucleus is removed (Tartar, 1961).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: Five Pumilio orthologs showed differential gene expression during regeneration.
source: Our differential expression analysis identified five Pumilio orthologs showing differential gene expression during regeneration, one specific to OA regeneration (cluster 2; SteCoe_27339; Figure 6A), one specific to tail regeneration (cluster 2; SteCoe_37495; Figure 6B), and three specific to the sucrose shock response (cluster 1; SteCoe_9692; cluster 2 SteCoe_16166; cluster 5; SteCoe_22534).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6A and B.

claim: Among the oral apparatus regeneration specific genes, 34 genes were found to be putative Pumilio targets.
source: Among the OA regeneration specific genes, 34 genes were found to be putative Pumilio targets (see Supplementary file 1), and these distinctly cluster into two groups with peaks of expression at 120 and 300 min respectively after the start of regeneration (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6E.

claim: Out of the 34 Pumilio target genes showing differential expression, none of them were contained in cluster 1 of the oral apparatus regeneration gene set.
source: Notably, out of the 34 Pumilio target genes showing differential expression, none of them were contained in cluster 1 of the OA regeneration gene set, the cluster that contains genes whose expression decreases during regeneration.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of Pumilio targets.

claim: 100% of the Pumilio targets showed increased rather than decreased expression during oral apparatus regeneration.
source: Thus, 100%of the Pumilio targets showed increased rather than decreased expression during OA regeneration.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of Pumilio targets.

claim: All of the predicted Pumilio targets showed reduced induction in cycloheximide-treated cells.
source: All of the predicted Pumilio targets showed reduced induction in cycloheximide-treated cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from cycloheximide experiments.

claim: RNAi of Pumilio had no effect on cell morphology in pre-shocked cells but caused a number of morphological abnormalities when cells regenerated after sucrose shock.
source: We observed that RNAi of this Pumilio ortholog had no effect on cell morphology in pre-shocked cells (Figure 6H) but caused a number of morphological abnormalities when cells regenerated after sucrose shock.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6H.

claim: The most common defect seen in Pumilio RNAi cells was that cells regenerated an abnormally small oral apparatus that was significantly smaller than the diameter of the cell.
source: The most common defect seen was that cells regenerated an abnormally small OA that was significantly smaller than the diameter of the cell (Figure 6I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6I.

claim: Regeneration represents a collection of distinct, part-specific processes rather than a single process that restores proper morphology following the loss of any part.
source: A classical question in regenerative biology is whether regeneration represents a single process that restores proper morphology following the loss of any part, or instead a collection of distinct, part-specific processes. Our comparative transcriptomic approach in Stentor clearly supports the latter view, in that we found regeneration genes could be decomposed into modules specific for different aspects of regeneration.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the comparative transcriptomic analysis.

claim: The fact that the general regeneration module contains the fewest genes out of all the modules identified suggests that regeneration does not represent a single 'master' program of expression, but rather a composite of distinct expression modules or subroutines specific for regenerating individual parts of the cell.
source: The fact that the general regeneration module contains the fewest genes out of all the modules identified suggests that regeneration does not represent a single 'master' program of expression, but rather a composite of distinct expression modules or subroutines specific for regenerating individual parts of the cell.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the modular organization.

claim: The fact that cycloheximide treatment had larger effects on later expressed groups of genes is more consistent with a cascade mechanism than a production schedule mechanism.
source: The fact that cycloheximide treatment had larger effects on later expressed groups of genes (Figure 4C and D) is thus more consistent with a cascade mechanism.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the cycloheximide results.

claim: E2F and other early-expressed genes whose expression does not require protein synthesis may be playing a role analogous to immediate early genes in regulating Stentor regeneration.
source: We propose that E2F and other early-expressed genes whose expression does not require protein synthesis may be playing an analogous role in regulating Stentor regeneration.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis based on comparison with other systems.

claim: The strong morphological similarity between regeneration and division, together with the expression of cell cycle and mitosis-related genes during regeneration, suggests the possibility that oral apparatus regeneration might involve co-option of parts of the cell cycle machinery to regulate the timing of events.
source: The strong morphological similarity between regeneration and division, at both the cortical and nuclear level, together with the expression of cell cycle and mitosis-related genes during regeneration, suggests the possibility that OA regeneration might involve co-option of parts of the cell cycle machinery to regulate the timing of events.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis based on morphological and expression similarities.

claim: An alternative explanation for the upregulation of cell cycle genes during regeneration could be that the micronuclei undergo mitosis during regeneration.
source: However, an alternative explanation for the upregulation of cell cycle genes during regeneration could be the fact that in Stentor, the micronuclei undergo mitosis during regeneration (Guttes and Guttes, 1959).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an alternative hypothesis with a citation.

claim: Out of 215 proteins identified as highly abundant components of isolated membranellar bands, 173 corresponded to genes upregulated during regeneration.
source: Out of 215 protein identified as highly abundance components of isolated MBs (Lin et al., 2022), 173 corresponded to genes upregulated during regeneration, while the other proteins were not detected in this study.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to prior work.

claim: At least some of the genes in clusters 2 and 3 with no or poor homology to known genes may encode undiscovered factors involved in centriole biogenesis and ciliogenesis.
source: Based on this positive correlation with known genes involved in centrioles and cilia, we predict that at least some of the genes in these clusters with no or poor homology to known genes may encode undiscovered factors involved in centriole biogenesis and ciliogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a prediction based on the correlation with known genes.

claim: Cluster 2 may contain genes whose products are needed for basal body assembly, or for positioning the oral apparatus in relation to other cellular structures, but may not encode structural components of the basal body itself.
source: In particular, while the proteome of the centriole/basal body has become increasingly well characterized (Keller et al., 2005; Jakobsen et al., 2011; Lauwaet et al., 2011; Firat-Karalar et al., 2014; Hamel et al., 2017), we hypothesize that cluster 2 may contain genes whose products are needed for basal body assembly, or for positioning the OA in relation to other cellular structures, but may not encode structural components of the basal body itself.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis with citations to prior work.

claim: The expression of LRRC45 at the stage when basal bodies associate into pairs and larger groups suggests that this linker may be a key element for assembling the membranellar band from the initially randomly oriented basal bodies.
source: The expression of LRRC45 at exactly this stage suggests that this linker may be a key element for assembling the MB from the initially randomly oriented basal bodies.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis based on timing of expression.

claim: Meckel and Joubert syndrome genes may be expressed during regeneration in order to equip the newly formed basal bodies with appropriate protein machinery to generate oral apparatus-specific cilia.
source: We hypothesize that these genes may be expressed during regeneration in order to equip the newly formed basal bodies with appropriate protein machinery to generate OA-specific cilia.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis about the function of ciliopathy genes.

claim: GAS2 may play a role in aligning the membranelles with the longitudinal microtubule bundles that define the ciliary rows on the cell body.
source: We hypothesize that GAS2 may play a role in aligning the membranelles with the longitudinal microtubule bundles that define the ciliary rows on the cell body.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis about GAS2 function.

claim: One possibility is that in posterior half-cells regenerating oral apparatus, assembly of motile cilia onto the basal bodies is carried out using protein obtained from either a pre-existing cytoplasmic pool or else from the pre-existing cilia on the cell body.
source: One possibility is that in these cells, assembly of motile cilia onto the basal bodies is carried out using protein obtained from either a pre-existing cytoplasmic pool or else from the pre-existing cilia on the cell body.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis to explain the lack of ciliary gene expression.

claim: It is possible that the larger size of the oral apparatus being formed after sucrose shock requires synthesis of new protein, existing pools being insufficient.
source: It is therefore possible that the larger size of the OA being formed after sucrose shock requires synthesis of new protein, existing pools being insufficient.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis about scaling.

claim: Carbonic anhydrase may act to increase the pH of cytoplasm after wound healing by dehydrating carbonic acid to CO2.
source: Carbonic anhydrase may act to increase the pH of cytoplasm after wound healing by dehydrating carbonic acid to CO2.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis about carbonic anhydrase function.

claim: The identification of Pumilio in the Stentor regeneration program suggests that there may be conserved molecular mechanisms at work during morphogenesis in both single-celled and multi-celled organisms.
source: The identification of Pumilio, a highly conserved developmental regulator (Wreden et al., 1997; Gamberi et al., 2002; Sonoda and Wharton, 1999) in the Stentor regeneration program, suggests that there may in fact be conserved molecular mechanisms at work during morphogenesis in both single-celled and multi-celled organisms.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to prior work.

claim: Some of the relevant Pumilio targets in other regeneration programs may be genes whose transcripts are already present prior to initiation of regeneration.
source: One potential explanation is that some of the relevant Pumilio targets in these other programs may be genes whose transcripts are already present prior to initiation of regeneration.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis to explain the lack of Pumilio targets in some modules.

claim: Stentor regeneration involves expression of regulatory genes conserved across eukaryotes, suggesting a deep conservation of developmental mechanisms.
source: We find that Stentor regeneration involves expression of regulatory genes conserved across eukaryotes, suggesting a deep conservation of developmental mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated in the Conclusion section as a summary of findings.

claim: The membranellar band is shed during sucrose shock at t=0.
source: At t=0,the membranellar band is shed during sucrose shock.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1A caption.

claim: One hour after the start of regeneration, basal bodies begin to form at the locus of stripe contrast.
source: One hour after the start of regeneration, basal bodies begin to form at the locus of stripe contrast.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1A caption.

claim: After 3 hours of regeneration, the first cilia of the new membranellar band are visible.
source: After 3 hr, the first cilia of the new membranellar band are visible.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1A caption.

claim: By 8 hours after sucrose shock the Stentor is fully regenerated.
source: By 8 hr after sucrose shock the Stentor is fully regenerated.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1A caption.

claim: Immediately after cutting, both half-cells heal their wounded edges.
source: Immediately after cutting, both half-cells heal their wounded edges.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1B caption.

claim: Oral regeneration in the posterior half-cell has the same general morphological events and timing as oral regeneration in the sucrose-shocked cells.
source: Oral regeneration in the posterior half-cell has the same general morphological events and timing as oral regeneration in the sucrose-shocked cells.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1B caption.

claim: The peak expression of each cluster of genes corresponds with major developmental features identified morphologically.
source: The peak expression of each cluster of genes corresponds with major developmental features identified morphologically (as described in Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 2A caption.

claim: In Chlamydomonas, radial spoke protein synthesis reaches its maximum rate 30–60 minutes after the flagella have begun assembling onto pre-existing basal bodies.
source: In Chlamydomonas, radial spoke protein synthesis reaches its maximum rate 30–60 min after the flagella have begun assembling onto pre-existing basal bodies (Remillard and Witman, 1982).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: This timing roughly matches the delay of 1 hour seen in the data between the peak expression of genes involved in ciliary assembly (cluster 2) and genes encoding radial spokes during Stentor regeneration (cluster 4).
source: This timing roughly matches the delay of 1 hr seen in our data between the peak expression of genes involved in ciliary assembly (cluster 2) and genes encoding radial spokes during Stentor regeneration (cluster 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a comparison with Chlamydomonas.

claim: The contractile vacuole can still regenerate in enucleated posterior half-cells.
source: The contractile vacuole can still regenerate in enucleated posterior half-cells (Stevens, 1903; Tartar, 1956), but this does not necessarily mean that contractile vacuole-related genes are not upregulated during normal regeneration.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claim: The number of genes upregulated during tail regeneration (13) is far smaller than the number upregulated during oral apparatus regeneration (564).
source: The number of genes upregulated during tail regeneration (13) is far smaller than the number upregulated during OA regeneration (564; Figure 2A clusters 2–5), consistent with the fact that the posterior holdfast can still regenerate in enucleated cells and therefore does not rely on transcription for its regeneration (Tartar, 1956).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: The posterior holdfast can still regenerate in enucleated cells and therefore does not rely on transcription for its regeneration.
source: The number of genes upregulated during tail regeneration (13) is far smaller than the number upregulated during OA regeneration (564; Figure 2A clusters 2–5), consistent with the fact that the posterior holdfast can still regenerate in enucleated cells and therefore does not rely on transcription for its regeneration (Tartar, 1956).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: Increased expression for many of the tail regeneration genes does not occur until at least 120 minutes, by which time the holdfast has already completely regenerated.
source: Increased expression for many of the tail regeneration genes does not occur until at least 120 min, by which time it has been reported that the holdfast has already completely regenerated (Morgan, 1901a; Weisz, 1951), suggesting that the upregulation of these genes is taking place after assembly, perhaps to regenerate depleted pools of precursor protein.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claim: The upregulation of tail regeneration genes is taking place after assembly, perhaps to regenerate depleted pools of precursor protein.
source: Increased expression for many of the tail regeneration genes does not occur until at least 120 min, by which time it has been reported that the holdfast has already completely regenerated (Morgan, 1901a; Weisz, 1951), suggesting that the upregulation of these genes is taking place after assembly, perhaps to regenerate depleted pools of precursor protein.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a hypothesis based on timing.

claim: Studies of cellular structure in Stentor showed that the posterior half of the cell contains long contractile fibers composed of centrin-like EF hand proteins.
source: Studies of cellular structure in Stentor showed that the posterior half of the cell contains long contractile fibers composed of centrin-like EF hand proteins (Huang, 1973; Maloney et al., 2005), and studies of cell movement showed that the contractile behavior of the cell, which is driven by these EF hand protein fibers, occurs primarily in the posterior half of the cell (Newman, 1972).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claim: The contractile behavior of the cell, which is driven by EF hand protein fibers, occurs primarily in the posterior half of the cell.
source: Studies of cellular structure in Stentor showed that the posterior half of the cell contains long contractile fibers composed of centrin-like EF hand proteins (Huang, 1973; Maloney et al., 2005), and studies of cell movement showed that the contractile behavior of the cell, which is driven by these EF hand protein fibers, occurs primarily in the posterior half of the cell (Newman, 1972).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claim: Cluster 2 of the bisection response (slow downregulation) contains a number of genes encoding protein classes similar to those seen in cluster 1 (rapid downregulation) of the oral apparatus-specific gene set.
source: We noted that cluster 2 of the bisection response (slow downregulation) contains a number of genes encoding protein classes similar to those seen in cluster 1 (rapid downregulation) of the OA-specific gene set.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation about gene similarity.

claim: This similarity suggests that similar genes are inactivated during regeneration in bisected and sucrose-shocked cells, but with slower kinetics of repression in the bisected cells.
source: This similarity suggests that similar genes are inactivated during regeneration in bisected and sucrose-shocked cells, but with slower kinetics of repression in the bisected cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the gene similarity.

claim: Changes in cytoplasmic pH have been reported following plasma membrane wounding or other forms of damage in animal cells.
source: Changes in cytoplasmic pH have been reported following plasma membrane wounding or other forms of damage in animal cells (Chambers and Chambers, 1961).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to prior work.

claim: Since Stentor grows in pond water that is relatively acidic, a wound in the plasma membrane is expected to cause acidification of the cytoplasm.
source: Since Stentor grows in pond water that is relatively acidic, a wound in the plasma membrane is expected to cause acidification of the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference based on the environment.

claim: The expression of a ABC transporter and a major facilitator superfamily member may indicate a role in pumping contaminants out of the cell that may have entered through the open wound.
source: Similarly, the expression of an ABC transporter and a major facilitator superfamily member, both of which are involved in transporting a wide range of small molecules out of cells (Wong et al., 2014; Quistgaard et al., 2016), may indicate a role in pumping contaminants out of the cell that may have entered through the open wound.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to prior work.

claim: Pumilio is a highly conserved developmental regulator that mediates mRNA localization and translation control during pattern formation in animal embryos such as Drosophila.
source: One of the most highly conserved developmental regulators in early animal development is the RNA-binding protein Pumilio, which mediates mRNA localization and translation control during pattern formation in animal embryos such as Drosophila (Wreden et al., 1997; Gamberi et al., 2002; Sonoda and Wharton, 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior work.

claim: These putative Pumilio orthologs all contain PUF domains based on Pfam analysis.
source: These putative Pumilio orthologs all contain PUF domains based on Pfam analysis, and phylogenetic analysis groups them together with bona fide Pumilio orthologs in animals (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6C.

claim: Phylogenetic analysis groups the Stentor Pumilio orthologs together with bona fide Pumilio orthologs in animals.
source: These putative Pumilio orthologs all contain PUF domains based on Pfam analysis, and phylogenetic analysis groups them together with bona fide Pumilio orthologs in animals (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6C.

claim: Among the OA regeneration specific genes, 34 genes were found to be putative Pumilio targets, and these distinctly cluster into two groups with peaks of expression at 120 and 300 minutes respectively after the start of regeneration.
source: Among the OA regeneration specific genes, 34 genes were found to be putative Pumilio targets (see Supplementary file 1), and these distinctly cluster into two groups with peaks of expression at 120 and 300 min respectively after the start of regeneration (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6E.

claim: The timing of the peaks of Pumilio target expression coincides with the peak expression of Pumilio orthologs.
source: The timing of these peaks coincides with the peak expression of Pumilio orthologs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation about timing.

claim: Sixteen of the 34 predicted Pumilio targets showed recognizable homology, and out of these, six were either kinases or phosphatases.
source: Sixteen of the 34 predicted targets showed recognizable homology, and out of these, six were either kinases or phosphatases, which we speculate may potentially suggest a role for Pumilio in regulating mRNA encoding proteins of signaling pathways that regulate later steps of morphogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of Pumilio targets.

claim: Pumilio may play a role in regulating mRNA encoding proteins of signaling pathways that regulate later steps of morphogenesis.
source: Sixteen of the 34 predicted targets showed recognizable homology, and out of these, six were either kinases or phosphatases, which we speculate may potentially suggest a role for Pumilio in regulating mRNA encoding proteins of signaling pathways that regulate later steps of morphogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as speculation based on the types of targets.

claim: Four Pumilio targets corresponded to basal body-associated proteins.
source: Another four targets corresponded to basal body-associated proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from analysis of Pumilio targets.

claim: RNAi of Pumilio ortholog SteCoe_27339 had no effect on cell morphology in pre-shocked cells.
source: We observed that RNAi of this Pumilio ortholog had no effect on cell morphology in pre-shocked cells (Figure 6H) but caused a number of morphological abnormalities when cells regenerated after sucrose shock.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6H.

claim: Another defect seen in some Pumilio RNAi cells was a failure to build an oral apparatus at all, such that some cells had a primordium located on the side of the cell that failed to migrate to the anterior end.
source: Another defect seen in some cells was a failure to build an OA at all, such that some cells had a primordium located on the side of the cell that failed to migrate to the anterior end (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Other less frequent phenotypes in Pumilio RNAi cells were the presence of two posterior tails, cells having an abnormal rounded appearance, and dead cells showing a rupture of the cell and spilling of cytoplasm.
source: Other, less frequent phenotypes were the presence of two posterior tails (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), cells having an abnormal rounded appearance rather than the usual elongate Stentor cell shape (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C), and dead cells showing a rupture of the cell and spilling of cytoplasm (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to Figure 6—figure supplement 1 panels.

claim: The same set of phenotypes were seen across multiple Pumilio RNAi experiments.
source: The result of the individual experiments is given in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 panels E–G, which shows that the same set of phenotypes were seen across multiple experiments.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 1 panels E–G.

claim: When a Stentor cell is cut in half perpendicular to the long axis, two cell fragments are produced, an anterior half-cell and a posterior half-cell.
source: When a Stentor cell is cut in half perpendicular to the long axis, two cell fragments are produced, an anterior half-cell and a posterior half-cell.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1B caption.

claim: The anterior half-cell regenerates a new posterior body including the hold-fast.
source: The anterior half-cell then regenerates a new posterior body including the hold-fast, and the posterior half-cell regenerates a new anterior body including the oral apparatus (OA).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1B caption.

claim: The posterior half-cell regenerates a new anterior body including the oral apparatus.
source: The anterior half-cell then regenerates a new posterior body including the hold-fast, and the posterior half-cell regenerates a new anterior body including the oral apparatus (OA).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1B caption.

claim: Stentor cells were obtained from Carolina Biological Supply and cultured in Pasteurized Spring Water and fed with Chlamydomonas and wheat seeds.
source: Cells were obtained from Carolina Biological Supply (cat. num. 131598) and cultured as previously described (Slabodnick et al., 2013). Cells were maintained in Pasteurized Spring Water (Carolina Biological Supply) and fed with Chlamydomonas and wheat seeds.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: To induce regeneration of the oral apparatus by sucrose shock, cells were placed in a 15% sucrose solution for 2 minutes.
source: To induce regeneration of the OA by sucrose shock (Lin et al., 2018), cells were placed in a 15% sucrose solution for 2 min (Tartar, 1957), and then washed in Carolina Spring Water thoroughly.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citations.

claim: Samples of approximately 20 cells were collected before shock, then at 30 minutes post shock, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 hours.
source: Samples of ~20 cells were collected before shock, then at 30 min post shock, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 hr.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Four replicates were analyzed for each time point in the sucrose shock experiments.
source: Four replicates were analyzed for each time point.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: RNA was extracted at each time point using the Nucleospin RNA XS kit from Clontech.
source: RNA was extracted at each time point using the Nucleospin RNA XS kit from Clontech (cat. num. 740902.250).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: RNAseq libraries were prepared with Ovation RNAseq system v2 kit.
source: RNAseq libraries were prepared with Ovation RNAseq system v2 kit (NuGEN).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: High-throughput sequencing was done using a HiSeq 2500 instrument.
source: High-throughput sequencing was done using a HiSeq 2500 instrument (Illumina).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Libraries were paired-end sequenced with 100 base reads.
source: Libraries were paired-end sequenced with 100 base reads.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: RNAseq data from this study are available in GEO under accession number GSE186036.
source: RNAseq data from this study are available in GEO under accession number GSE186036.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Trimmomatic was used to trim RNAseq reads.
source: We used trimmomatic (Bolger et al., 2014) to trim RNAseq reads with the following flags: ILLUMINACLIP:$adapterfile:2:30:10 HEADCROP:6 MINLEN:22 AVGQUAL:20
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with a citation.

claim: To generate a transcriptome, all reads from all RNAseq samples and time points were combined.
source: To generate a transcriptome, we combined all the reads from all RNAseq samples and time points.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Tophat2 was run to align the reads to the genome.
source: We ran Tophat2 (Kim et al., 2013) to align the reads to the genome (StentorDB http://stentor.ciliate.org; Slabodnick et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citations.

claim: Trinity was run using a genome guided approach.
source: We then ran Trinity (Haas et al., 2013) using a genome guided approach.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with a citation.

claim: In total, 34,501 genes aligned with the existing Stentor genome models in StentorDB, plus 143 novel models were assembled.
source: In total, we assembled 34,501 genes aligned with the existing Stentor genome models in StentorDB, plus 143 novel models.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Kallisto was used to quantify transcript abundance.
source: We used Kallisto to quantify transcript abundance (Bray et al., 2016) using the following flags: -t 15 -b 30.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with a citation.

claim: Sleuth was used to identify genes which are differentially expressed genes through the regeneration time course.
source: We then used Sleuth (Pimentel et al., 2017) to identify genes which are differentially expressed genes through the regeneration time course.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with a citation.

claim: Nearly 5583 transcripts are differentially expressed during oral apparatus regeneration.
source: We found that nearly 5583 transcripts are differentially expressed during OA regeneration.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Of the differentially expressed transcripts, 485 had no clear homology to proteins in NCBI databases nor PFAM.
source: Of these, 485 had no clear homology to proteins in NCBI databases nor PFAM.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: 234 differentially expressed transcripts did not map to existing gene models.
source: We identified 234 that did not map to existing gene models.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: RNAi by feeding was performed as previously described.
source: RNAi by feeding was performed as previously described (Slabodnick et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with a citation.

claim: RNAi experiments are set up in 12-well plates with 2 ml of filtered spring water in each well.
source: Briefly, RNAi experiments are set up in 12-well plates with 2 ml of filtered spring water in each well.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Bacteria expressing the RNAi constructs were added to the well daily for 10 days.
source: Bacteria expressing the RNAi constructs were added to the well daily for 10 days, exchanging the media for fresh media half way through the experiment.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Images were acquired using a Zeiss Axiozoom microscope with a ×2.3 objective lens and total magnification of ×40 or ×80 using a Nikon Rebel T3i digital SLR camera.
source: Images were acquired using a Zeiss Axiozoom microscope with a ×2.3 objective lens and total magnification of ×40 or ×80 using a Nikon Rebel T3i digital SLR camera.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.
